newsitem.title: USA: OAS Chief calls for improved U.S.-Colombia ties.
newsitem.headline: OAS Chief calls for improved U.S.-Colombia ties.

text.p: Organisation of American States Secretary-General Cesar Gaviria called for an easing of tensions between Colombia and the United States so a more effective war against drugs could be waged.

Ties between Washington and Bogota have been strained since allegations emerged that Colombian President Ernesto Samper accepted funds from narcotics traffickers during his 1994 presidential campaign.

The Clinton administration decertified Colombia as a nation contributing to the war on drugs, which opened the nation to potential trade sanctions, and in July revoked Samper's visa to travel to the United States.

"I am very anxious to see that a climate of cooperation between Colombian and the United States can be established, particularly in the fight against narcotics trafficking," said Gaviria, a former president of Colombia.
"The policy of confrontation through which we have been living is one that doesn't serve any purpose of having an efficient policy," Gaviria added.
